final_answer: Special relativity establishes that the speed of light (c) is a universal constant, unattainable by any object with mass. As an object's velocity approaches c, its relativistic mass increases, requiring exponentially more energy to accelerate further. This energy requirement becomes infinite at c, making it impossible to reach or exceed the speed of light. Additionally, spacetime's structure ensures that the speed of light is the maximum possible velocity, as any attempt to surpass it would result in non-physical, imaginary values in the equations governing motion. Thus, the speed of light acts as an absolute limit, preserving the consistency of physical laws across all inertial frames.
